engineering_objective: Complete the inherited Terraform and Kubernetes EKS add-on trust rollout system so add-on controllers, IRSA subjects, PodDisruptionBudgets, node pool taints, and regulated workload placement achieve policy-compliant, interruption-safe upgrade readiness.
required_end_state: The Terraform workspace at /app/terraform, Kubernetes manifests under /app/k8s, and upgrade lab engine under /app/upgrade_lab correctly plan target add-on versions, enforce single-subject IRSA roles with narrow IAM policies, maintain required PodDisruptionBudgets during node drains, restrict regulated workloads to private on-demand node pools, advance add-ons in prerequisite order, and produce deterministic READY upgrade reports.
functional_requirements: Operate the upgrade system through the public operator CLI at /app/bin/addon-trust-rollout.

Validate that the Terraform plan at /app/var/upgrade/plan.json includes all required add-ons (vpc-cni, ebs-csi, coredns, kube-proxy, aws-load-balancer-controller, karpenter) matching exact target versions in /app/data/compatibility_matrix.json.
Enforce resolve_conflicts_on_update = 'PRESERVE' for all EKS add-ons in the Terraform plan.
Parse SSM parameter tags for controller add-ons to extract version overrides and conflict resolution settings.
Ensure each IRSA role in Terraform trusts exactly one service account subject matching /app/data/trust_observations.json and rejects wildcards or forbidden subjects (e.g. system:nodes).
Verify that IAM role policy statements contain no wildcard actions (* or ebs:*) and that role names match expected naming conventions.
Validate that submitted Kubernetes manifests under /app/k8s supply required PodDisruptionBudgets matching names, namespaces, and minAvailable thresholds in /app/data/pdbs.json.
Verify that the system node group retains CriticalAddonsOnly=true:NoSchedule taints and correct nodepool labels.
Simulate system node draining while respecting PodDisruptionBudget minAvailable limits and tracking core service availability.
Enforce explicit nodepool selectors and capacity-type constraints for regulated workloads, restricting them to private on-demand node pools.
Verify Karpenter NodePool CRD specifications to ensure regulated capacity requirements exclude spot instances.
Simulate spot/on-demand node interruptions and verify that regulated workloads remain on on-demand capacity after rebalancing.
Validate add-on rollout prerequisites before advancing each add-on, rolling out add-ons in exact compatibility matrix order.
Verify add-on readiness before marking each step complete and report status = READY only when all readiness conditions pass.
Audit cross-service trust to ensure no IAM role ARN is shared across distinct add-ons.
Merge inline role policies and standalone role policy attachments in plan normalization.
Strictly guard resources tagged UpgradeProtected=true against delete or replace actions in the Terraform plan.
Record step-by-step rollout state checkpoints to enable atomic restart recovery upon interruption.
Publish deterministic reports to /app/output/upgrade-report.json with canonical formatting, sorted keys, stable semantic fields, and repeatable SHA-256 report digests.
preservation_requirements: Preserve documented CLI entrypoint /app/bin/addon-trust-rollout, report schema, and plan path /app/var/upgrade/plan.json.
Keep the Python upgrade_lab, Terraform workspace structure, and Kubernetes manifest boundaries intact.
Do not mutate cluster snapshot data or test fixtures outside documented state and output paths.
compatibility_requirements: Maintain compatibility with datasets under /app/data, manifests under /app/k8s, and Terraform files under /app/terraform.
Treat technical contract at /app/docs/addon-trust-rollout-contract.md as binding.
Generate 12,500 deterministic synthetic primary records across cluster snapshots, trust observations, telemetry, matrix entries, and interruption events without live AWS calls.
safety_requirements: Deterministic execution must use the local upgrade lab and must not contact live AWS APIs or Kubernetes clusters.
Never leak credentials or volatile runtime facts into output reports or state checkpoints.
Policy violations, missing add-ons, or malformed manifests must fail closed with clear error reasons without corrupting state.

required_outputs.notes: Deterministic upgrade readiness report with stable semantic fields and SHA-256 digest.
